page.overview:
Who is Yin Wenjiao?

Yin Wenjiao was the daughter of the chief minister of Chang'an. When he saw Chen Guangrui, who was being paraded around after passing the imperial examination with the highest grade, she fell in love with him instantly. She sent her attendants out to collect him, then had her father marry them that day.

The following day, Wenjiao accompanied her husband to his new position in Jiangzhou. While they were crossing the Hong River, the ferryman Liu Hong murdered Guangrui and forced Wenjiao to be his wife. She did so out of fear for her unborn child.

When her child was born, she was instructed in a dream by the Old Man of the South Pole to set him adrift on the river. She wrote her baby's lineage on his bundle, then bit off part of one of his toes so she could identify them.

Several years later, she reunited with her son, now a monk named Xuanzang. After confirming his identity, she had Xuanzang send a letter to her father, who arrested and executed Liu Hong. Sadly, she later committed suicide, still filled with grief for having had to pretend Liu Hong was her husband for several years.
